# AI Native Software Engineering Workshop

> A full-day interactive workshop teaching software developers how to work effectively with AI tools. Covers everything from LLM fundamentals to capability-first agentic workflows across Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, and Devin Desktop. Built and presented by Jan De Dobbeleer (Engineering Leader & Open Source Innovator).

**Audience:** Software developers of all levels. No prior AI experience required — comfortable with software development is enough.

**Format:** Full-day, instructor-led, hands-on. Delivered as a web-based interactive slideshow at [https://ainativedev.itdepends.be](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be). Navigation is sequential (slide by slide) with the ability to jump to any section. The source code is available at [https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/workshop_ai_native](https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/workshop_ai_native).

**Note for agents:** The slideshow is password-protected (lightweight SHA-256 client-side gate). Public static assets available without authentication: `llms.txt` (this file), `llms-full.txt`, `favicon.svg`, `og-image.png`, `robots.txt`, and `sitemap.xml`.

## Workshop Sections

- [Introduction](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Workshop overview, the AI-native developer mindset, and the "quantum state" of AI adoption — how developers simultaneously exist across multiple adoption stages
- [LLMs](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): How large language models actually work — transformers, tokenisation, context windows, hallucinations, and GPU acceleration
- [AI Fluency](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): The 4D framework for effective AI collaboration — Delegation (when to engage AI), Description (communicating goals clearly), Discernment (evaluating AI outputs critically), Diligence (taking responsibility for AI use). Three interaction modes: Augmentation, Automation, Agency
- [Prompting](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): The art of communicating with AI — prompt engineering patterns, chain-of-thought, few-shot examples, and avoiding common mistakes
- [Models](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Choosing the right model for the job — the model landscape, capability vs cost tradeoffs, reasoning models, and when to use each
- [Instructions](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Persistent guidance — cross-tool config paths, AGENTS.md, scoped rules, comparison matrices
- [Agents & Skills](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Two portable layers (`AGENTS.md` + `.agents/skills/` — skills-only), custom agents, skills, delegation — cross-tool matrix with per-tool gaps
- [Context](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Context engineering — attach syntax, indexing, implicit vs explicit context
- [Spec Driven Development](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Making technical decisions explicit, reviewable, and executable — writing specs before coding, using AI to validate and implement from specs
- [Security](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Risks and best practices for secure AI-assisted coding — OWASP Top 10, prompt injection, insecure code generation, and mitigation strategies
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): The universal standard for connecting AI to external systems — MCP servers, tools, resources, and how to expose your own APIs to AI
- [Team Knowledge](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Shared knowledge bases and team-wide AI configuration — Copilot Spaces, APM, shared instruction repos
- [Terminal Agents](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): CLI entry points across tools — Copilot CLI deep dive, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Devin Desktop
- [Multi-Agent](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Parallel orchestration — define/delegate/parallelize/isolate/synthesize, worktrees, and when multi-agent helps vs hurts
- [Closing](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Workshop summary, next steps, and feedback

## Optional / Addendum

- [Ollama](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Running AI models locally — transforming AI accessibility, local inference, and use cases for on-device models
- [Agent SDKs](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): Programmatic agent runtimes — Copilot SDK primary, gaps for other vendors
- [Evolution of the Programmer](https://ainativedev.itdepends.be): The 8 stages from traditional developer to AI-native engineer

- [Source code](https://github.com/JanDeDobbeleer/workshop_ai_native): React + TypeScript + Tailwind slideshow. Each section is a self-contained component under `src/sections/`
- [Slide Content Creator agent](.github/agents/create-section.md): Custom agent definition used to generate new slide sections from source material

## Key Concepts

Core mental models taught in the workshop, useful for answering questions about its content:

- **Quantum State of Adoption** — AI is unique in that developers simultaneously exist across multiple stages of the technology adoption lifecycle, rather than moving through them sequentially
- **4D Fluency Framework** — Four competencies for AI collaboration: *Delegation* (deciding when/how to engage AI), *Description* (communicating effectively), *Discernment* (evaluating outputs critically), *Diligence* (taking responsibility for AI-assisted work)
- **Three AI Interaction Modes** — *Augmentation* (human and AI collaborate), *Automation* (AI executes specific tasks), *Agency* (AI acts independently on future tasks)
- **Agent Loop** — The repeating cycle of: LLM receives context → decides on tool call → tool executes → result fed back to LLM → repeat. Underpins all agentic AI behaviour
- **Spec-Driven Development (SDD)** — Writing an explicit specification document before writing code. Makes assumptions reviewable, aligns teams and AI agents, documents the "why" not just the "what", and prevents costly rewrites from divergent assumptions
- **Two Portable Layers** — *Instructions:* root `AGENTS.md` (file, not `.agents/` folder). *Skills:* `.agents/skills/` where tools support it — partial portability only; agents, rules, and MCP remain tool-native
- **Agent vs Skill** — An *agent* defines *what is demanded* of the AI for a task (tool-native paths such as `.cursor/agents/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.github/agents/`). A *skill* (`SKILL.md` bundles in `.agents/skills/` or tool-native skills folders) defines *how to execute* it step by step. Skills are reusable across agents; agents can be chained
- **Pro Tool Stack principle** — Cheap/repetitive tasks → fast local models (Ollama). Complex reasoning → frontier cloud (Claude, GPT, Gemini). Sensitive/regulated code → private on-premises infrastructure

## Tools & Resources

External tools and resources referenced throughout the workshop:

- [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot): The primary AI coding tool covered in the workshop
- [GitHub Copilot CLI docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/use-copilot-cli): Official docs for the standalone `copilot` CLI agent
- [Ollama](https://ollama.ai): Run large language models locally
- [OpenCode CLI](https://opencode.ai): Open-source terminal AI agent supporting 75+ LLM providers
- [Wispr Flow](https://wisprflow.ai): Voice-to-text for developers — dictate prompts at 220 wpm
- [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io): Open standard for connecting AI to external systems (tools, data sources)
- [OWASP Top 10](https://owasp.org/www-project-top-ten/): Security risk reference used in the Security section
- [llms.txt spec](https://llmstxt.org): The standard this file follows
